components: Each request timestamp is stored in an ordered per-key log.
The current time minus the interval defines the rolling boundary.
Timestamps older than the boundary are removed.
The remaining entries give the precise rolling request count.
The next request is accepted only when the count is below the limit.

lesson.scenario: An authentication endpoint permits five attempts in the exact trailing ten-second interval.
entities: Removes timestamps at or before the cutoff
Compares retained count with limit five
connections: evict timestamps at or before cutoff

steps.title: Four retained attempts
steps.narration: At 20.0 seconds, timestamps 11.0, 13.0, 17.0, and 19.0 are inside the window.
steps.outcome: One additional attempt can be admitted.
steps.invariant: Only timestamps greater than the exact cutoff count.

steps.title: Fifth admitted
steps.narration: The gate appends the attempt at 20.0 seconds.
steps.outcome: The exact trailing window is now full.
steps.invariant: Check and append must be atomic for one limiter key.

steps.title: Sixth rejected
steps.narration: At 20.1 seconds, all five prior timestamps remain in the window.
steps.outcome: The limiter rejects without recording an admitted timestamp.
steps.invariant: Rejected attempts are counted only if the product policy explicitly requires it.

steps.title: Oldest expires
steps.narration: At 21.1 seconds, timestamp 11.0 is outside the trailing window.
steps.outcome: Capacity opens exactly when the oldest admitted attempt expires.
steps.invariant: Boundary semantics must be consistent: this policy retains timestamps strictly newer than the cutoff.

steps.title: Next attempt admitted
steps.narration: The 21.1-second attempt is appended as the new fifth record.
steps.outcome: The rolling log enforces the exact interval without fixed-window boundary bursts.
steps.invariant: Exact sliding logs cost memory and ordered timestamp operations proportional to admitted traffic.

production.scenario: A retail banking login API enforces exact trailing ten-minute attempt limits per account to stop OTP brute force attacks without minute-boundary bursts.
components: submits password and OTP login attempts for retail customers
owns credential verification entry for consumer banking
publishes exact-window caps per account risk tier
tracks the exact trailing attempt budget for each account and IP
authoritative login execution path for requests allowed by the limiter
stores limiter shard checkpoints consumed by replacement login limiter pods
captures repeated blocks for analyst triage
flows: A customer submits a login attempt while the account is under elevated fraud monitoring.
The API loads the active attempt contract for the account and source network.
apply 5 attempts per 10m on account+ip key
The exact-window gate is updated with the current fraud rule before evaluation.
The request is checked against the trailing ten-minute history instead of a coarse bucket.
Only admitted attempts reach the authoritative password and OTP verification path.
Checkpoint metadata keeps the same account partition recoverable after pod movement.
Repeated blocks are surfaced to analysts with the offending account and source context.
